odd_even.verdict_text: The two dips match — odd transits dip 0.192% and even transits dip 0.201%, within 5% of each other. That is what a real planet crossing the same star every 1.46 days should look like.

double_period.verdict_text: The light between the eclipses is not flat — at the quarter-orbit points the system brightens to 1.0087 while the shoulders beside the eclipses sit at 1.0000: a 0.87% wave at 92σ. That brightening is two stars squeezed out of round by each other's gravity, showing us their wider sides twice per orbit — a planet is far too light to bend its star like this. These are twin stars orbiting every 2.91 days, not a planet.
